records.name: Camp Jamison
records.summary: A one-week overnight summer camp for kids 8 to 15 from the Philadelphia area. Campers hike, swim, paddle on the lake, play sports, make art, and sit around the campfire.
records.what_you_do: Campers spend a week at camp in the summer. Counselors and volunteers help run the week, and donors can help fund campers through a memorial scholarship.

schedule.text: One week of overnight camp each summer. The 2026 session was set for July 19 to 25, with an extension to July 29.

cost.text: The camp describes its fee as affordable and helps fund campers through a memorial scholarship. The exact fee was not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Use the online sign-up form on campjamison.org to register for the summer session, or join the waiting list for updates.
first_step.basis: Registration is open to kids 8 to 15 through a public form, though the site also mentions a waiting list.

records.notes: IRS legal name Camp Jamison Corporation. The newest dated item is a news post about 2026 applications, dated April 16, 2026, found on the homepage. The IRS filing address (9251 Woodenbridge Rd, 19114) is not published as a camp location because the page does not say where camp is held. Camp site and exact fee not confirmed.

records.name: The Irish Society of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that keeps Irish heritage alive through banquets, meetups and other events. Members and friends gather for the calendar of events, including a yearly Christmas party.
records.what_you_do: Attend a calendar event such as a banquet or meetup, or apply for membership through the site.

schedule.text: Events are listed on the group's calendar. The newest dated event on the site is the 2026 Annual Christmas Party on December 18, 2026, at the Ashburner Inn.

cost.text: Membership dues and event prices were not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Check the calendar for an event, then use the Contact link on the site to ask about attending. The Apply Now link starts membership.
first_step.basis: Calendar events are listed for the public, though the site does not say whether non-members can attend.

records.notes: IRS legal name is Irish Society. The newest date on the site is a scheduled December 18, 2026 event, and the page shows no posting dates, so the active status rests on a future event listing. Membership is by application and eligibility is not stated. No email or phone was shown on the page. The IRS filing address (12800 Townsend Rd, 19154) is not used because it is not a listed event site.

records.name: Polish People's University
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that has offered free lectures on Polish history, culture and tradition for more than 100 years. Anyone can attend the monthly talks from October to April, in person or on Zoom.
records.what_you_do: Attend a monthly lecture, watch past talks on the group's YouTube channel, or join the mailing list for event news.

schedule.text: Monthly lectures from October to April. A lecture is already listed for April 18, 2027 at 3 pm.

cost.text: Lectures are free. Donations are welcome and are tax deductible.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list on the site, then come to the next lecture at the Associated Polish Home on Academy Road, or join by Zoom when offered.
first_step.basis: Lectures are free and open to everyone, with a clear way to attend in person or online.

records.notes: IRS legal name Polski Uniwersytet Ludowy. The IRS list had the website typed as 'https: www.polishpeoplesuniversity.org', which is malformed. The corrected domain is the group's own site and matches its name. The March 15, 2026 lecture is the last past lecture listed. The April 18, 2027 lecture is a scheduled listing.

records.notes: Not verified. Both www.adderleyfoundation.org and adderleyfoundation.org returned HTTP 404. The name suggests a foundation, and private foundations are out of scope, so this needs a check before it is shown. Not searched: the two searches went to National Reentry and Generation Music.

records.name: Alpha Pi of Alpha Epsilon Pi
records.notes: Not verified. The IRS list's website field was 'Alpha Pi', which is a name and not an address. Not searched because the search budget was spent. The name suggests a Greek-letter fraternity chapter, which may be members only. Check before it is shown.

records.name: American Center for Asian Students
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports Asian American students on college campuses with career fairs, cultural events and networking. Its events have been held in Philadelphia, though the site does not list a local office or chapter.
records.what_you_do: Attend a career fair, cultural event or networking program, or contact the group to ask how students join.

schedule.text: Events are posted by date. The newest dated event on the site is a spring 2025 career fair on April 18, 2025.

cost.text: Event prices were not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page on asianstudents.org to ask how students join and whether a Philadelphia event is coming up.
first_step.basis: The site invites students to join but does not explain how membership works, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: IRS legal name American Center for Chinese Students Inc, also known as American Center for Asian Students. The IRS address is in Philadelphia, but the site lists no local office. The About page copyright says 2023 and an image path says March 2024; neither counts as evidence. Philadelphia events found on the site: an October 22, 2022 summit, a March 4, 2023 Flower Show pavilion, and an April 18, 2025 career fair at TUCC Philadelphia. Membership and eligibility are not stated, and current Philadelphia activity is not confirmed.

records.name: Block by Block Philly
records.summary: A volunteer-run nonprofit that organizes cleanups against litter and illegal dumping across Philadelphia. It also hosts block parties and works with schools and businesses on clean streets.
records.what_you_do: Join a listed cleanup, organize a cleanup with your own group, or clean your own block and submit your bags through the site's trash form.

schedule.text: Organized cleanups are listed on the site. The 4th Annual Train Tracks Cleanup is Saturday, October 10, 10 am to 12 noon, meeting at 30th and Pennsylvania Ave.

cost.text: Free to join. Donations and sponsorships are optional.

first_step.how: Show up at 30th and Pennsylvania Ave on Saturday, October 10 at 10 am for the Train Tracks Cleanup, or pick another cleanup from the site's event list. The group recommends 18 and up for the train tracks work.
first_step.basis: The site says volunteers of all ages and abilities are welcome at most events and explains how to join a listed cleanup.

records.notes: IRS legal name Block by Block Community. The Train Tracks post does not print the year. The 2026 Clean-Off banner and the Saturday, October 10 date both point to 2026. The contact page is blockbyblockphilly.org/contact. Donations go through PayPal and are not recorded here.

records.name: Charlie's Army Animal Rescue
records.summary: A small Philadelphia rescue that takes in stray and abandoned cats and kittens, gets them medical care, and finds them homes. It depends on foster homes, adopters and donors.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat or kitten until it is ready for adoption, help with transport, or donate. You can also adopt an animal from the rescue.

cost.text: Adoption fees, donation amounts and volunteer requirements were not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer link on charliesarmy.com to ask about fostering or transport, since the site lists those roles.
first_step.basis: The site lists volunteer roles and a clear Volunteer link, though it does not explain the Apply link or what the rescue requires.

records.notes: The site shows no dated items, so status is probably_active on the working-site rule. The IRS filing address is an apartment, so it is not published. Facebook and Instagram handles were taken from the site.

records.name: Generation Music
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that gives free music classes and workshops to students with little access to music. It was started in 2018 by two friends and is run in a youth-driven way.
records.what_you_do: Students take free music classes and workshops, and the group's volunteers and staff help run them. The listing does not explain how to volunteer or enroll.

cost.text: All programs are free, according to the listing.

first_step.how: Email info@generationmusic.art to ask about the next free class or workshop. The listing does not say how students enroll.
first_step.basis: Programs are free, but the listing does not say how to enroll, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The group's own website returned HTTP 404 at both addresses, so its details come from a Generocity listing, a public directory. The listing's executive director matches the IRS contact name. The only item found is a 2024 annual report with no posting date shown, so the status is unknown. The instrument_lessons tag is the closest fit for classroom music education. The IRS filing address is an apartment and is not published.

records.name: Helping Hands Nonprofit Organization
records.notes: Not verified. The typed website Helpinghandsnonprofitorganization.com returned HTTP 404 at both the bare and www addresses. The name is generic and the search budget was spent, so no public page was found. Check before it is shown.

records.name: MAAS Building
records.summary: An arts venue in North Philadelphia that runs the MAAS Presents concert series, rents its spaces, and runs resident artist and community programs. The public can attend shows, take classes, and perform there.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to a MAAS Presents show, or sign up for the newsletter. To take a class, perform, or rehearse at the venue, check the Rates page.

schedule.text: Concerts and events are posted on the site. Listed dates include October 22 and October 25, 2026, and a MAAS Presents show on December 9, 2026.

cost.text: Ticket prices vary by show and were not shown on the page. Rental and class rates are on the Rates page.

first_step.how: Pick an upcoming show on the site, such as the October 22 or October 25 events, and buy a ticket. To take a class or perform, check the Rates page.
first_step.basis: Public events are listed for anyone to attend, and the site invites people to perform or take classes.

records.notes: A venue and concert series, not a membership group. Verdict publish because the public can attend events and take classes or perform through its programs. IRS legal name Maas Presents. The IRS filing address (1320 N 5th St) differs from the venue address on the site (1325 N Randolph St), so the site address is used. The site lists no phone or email, only a Contact page link. The newest dates shown are upcoming events, so last_sign_of_life uses the newest listed date.

records.name: New Meridian Arts
records.notes: A literary publisher. The public way in is manuscript submission and buying books. No class, membership, volunteer or community program was found. The only date is a 2022 footer copyright, which does not count as evidence. Under the tier 1 rule, a company with no community program is not_a_group.

records.name: Philadelphia Council for Business Economics
records.notes: Not verified. The typed website www.pcbe.org:8080 returned a TLS error, and https://www.pcbe.org refused the connection. Not searched because the search budget was spent. The name suggests a business or professional group, which may be members only or out of scope. Check before it is shown.

records.name: National Reentry Workforce Collaborative
records.notes: A national network of reentry workforce providers, advocates and employers, with members in many cities. The IRS list's website field was the group's name, so the site was found by search and then read directly. The newest item is a certification notice posted October 8, 2026, and its 2026 conference is in New Orleans (October 20 to 23). The Philadelphia tie is a private mailbox on the IRS filing and a 2023 conference held in Philadelphia. No Philadelphia program or event was found, so the verdict is out_of_area. Revisit if a Philadelphia program is confirmed.

records.name: Ferasha Films
records.summary: A volunteer-run documentary film group in the Philadelphia area. It makes short films for causes, organizations and communities, and filmmakers with a story that fits its mission can apply.
records.what_you_do: Filmmakers and organizations can apply through the Story Application page, and anyone can donate. The site does not describe a volunteer sign-up or how the camera kids program works.

cost.text: Donations are accepted. Fees for filmmaker applications were not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Email hey@ferashafilms.com to ask how to volunteer or join the camera kids program, since the site does not describe either. Filmmakers can start on the Story Application page.
first_step.basis: Filmmakers must apply before anyone sees what the work is like, and volunteer routes are not explained.

records.notes: The only dated item on the site is a 2020 copyright line in the footer, which does not count as evidence. The film dates shown (2011 to 2012) are older project dates, so the status is unknown. The site says its newsletter signup may not be working yet.

notes: The batch held 15 groups, not 10. Used both searches (National Reentry, Generation Music) and 21 fetches. Four groups were not searched because the budget ran out: Adderley Foundation, Alpha Pi of Alpha Epsilon Pi, Helping Hands Nonprofit Organization, and Philadelphia Council for Business Economics. Their records are placeholders (verdict publish, status unknown, low confidence, no summary), so the publish step should hold them back until a re-run supplies the required fields. Needs a second look: Ferasha Films and Generation Music, both with unknown status. Dead or unreachable addresses are listed in blocked. No 403s, bot checks or rate limiting were seen. National Reentry is out_of_area, not a Philadelphia program.
